subject: Chemistry
title: Helium: Found on the Sun First
description: A 60-second lesson on Helium: Found on the Sun First.

hook.text: Helium was discovered on the Sun 27 years before anyone found it on Earth.

buildup.text: During an 1868 solar eclipse, astronomers saw an unknown yellow line in the Sun's spectrum.

discovery.text: They named the mystery element helium, from 'helios'—Greek for Sun. Nobody had ever seen it on Earth.

twist.text: In 1895, William Ramsay found helium trapped in uranium ore. The Sun's element was here all along.

climax.text: Helium is the second most abundant element in the universe—but rare on Earth because it escapes to space.

punchline.text: Found on the Sun first. Rare on Earth because it floats away.

quiz.question: How was helium first discovered?
options: By observing an unknown spectral line during a solar eclipse
By cooling air to extremely low temperatures

details.summary: Helium was discovered spectroscopically on the Sun in 1868 by Pierre Janssen and Joseph Norman Lockyer, who observed an unknown yellow spectral line during a solar eclipse..
details.whyItMatters: Helium's solar discovery demonstrated that spectroscopy could identify elements across cosmic distances. Today helium is essential for cryogenics, MRI machines, and scientific research.
takeaways: Helium was identified on the Sun 27 years before being found on Earth
Spectroscopy revealed its unique yellow line during a solar eclipse
Helium is the only element discovered extraterrestrially before terrestrially

faq.question: How could scientists identify an element on the Sun before finding it on Earth?
faq.answer: Each element produces unique spectral lines when its atoms emit light. During the 1868 solar eclipse, astronomers observed a bright yellow line that matched no known element. They named the unknown element helium from helios, the Greek word for Sun..

faq.question: Why is there a helium shortage on Earth despite its cosmic abundance?
faq.answer: Helium is the second most abundant element in the universe but rare on Earth because it is too light for Earth's gravity to retain. Earth's helium comes from radioactive decay of uranium and thorium underground..
